q: Should I subtract brokerage when calculating position size?

a: Risk per trade is the budget — the rupees you are willing to lose if the stop is hit. Position size is what that budget buys: shares = risk budget ÷ stop distance. Two traders can risk the identical ₹1,000 while holding wildly different sizes, because their stops differ. Confusing the two is how traders end up 'risking 1%' while deploying 80% of their account on a wide stop — the risk number was right, the size was not.
